newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - March 31.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - March 31.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** India hurtles into political crisis on Sunday after the Congress party abruptly withdraws pivotal support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 10-month coalition government
The shock move by the nation's oldest party casts doubts over crucial talks between India and Pakistan and sends stock prices reeling

** Congress president Sitaram Kesri, citing what he calls growing lawlessness and a drifting economy, tells President Shankar Dayal Sharma that his party could no longer offer make-or-break backing for Deve Gowda's centre-left government
** Congress party's bold grab for power by seeking to topple Deve Gowda could backfire on the fractious party, analysts say
** The turmoil has placed a big question mark over some looming economic decisions, business leaders say

"We will have to wait and watch. Politics comes into focus and economics goes into background. There will be some uncertainty," says V. Raghuraman, the secretary general of Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (Assocham)
** Congress party's surprise withdrawal of support drives shares sharply lower in off-market kerb deals across the country on Sunday
Shares of leading firms Reliance Industries and State Bank of India plunge by an average four percent in off-market deals in Bombay, New Delhi and Calcutta
** United Front alliance says that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda will not resign but face parliament when it re-convenes on April 21
** Former finance minister and Congress leader Manmohan Singh says that a change in government should not deter foreign investors
Congress party says it might amend some budget proposals of Deve Gowda's government if the party succeeds in its declared bid to head a new coalition
Congress general secretary Ghulam Nabi Azad told Reuters: "We will see what changes are needed and implement them"

** Indian and Pakistani diplomats hold a third day of talks on Sunday even as political crisis threatens the future of the government in New Delhi and fresh violence flares in disputed region of Kashmir
** ANZ Grindlays wins $240 million award against National Housing Bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India in a case relating to the 1992 securities scandal
** Bombay Stock Exchange index ends Friday 72.05 points, or 1.93 percent, down at 3,663.53
** Indian rupee ends Thursday at 35.89/90 per dollar against opening 35.91/93. Banks were closed on Good Friday.
